posts.title: The Murder of Petersburg Anti-Fascist Timur Kacharava: 21 Years Later
posts.description: What can I say? Twenty-one years ago, a lovely young man named Timur Kacharava—a philosophy major at St. Petersburg State University, a punk rock musician, a Food Not Bombs activist, an anti-fascist—was murdered in cold blood by a band of neo-Nazis a few blocks from my house. Of course it was a sign of much worse things to come.

posts.title: Varieties of Censorship
posts.description: "When was the last time a book changed your life?": three tales, from the past and the present, of banned books in the U.S., Russia, and Ukraine.

posts.title: The Needle and the Damage Done
posts.description: Manifesting like an addiction, there is a certain species of leftism that bends so far toward the far right that it makes common cause with it, blaming "neoliberalism" and the U.S. for everything bad in the world, including Russia's brutal, unprovoked invasion of Ukraine.
